principles: Schemas match the spec EXACTLY (the acceptance is no downstream schema change).
Types + interface only, zero behavior, so S1-S4 build in parallel against a stable surface.
Declare the canonical round order as a single constant so S1-S4 cannot drift from sections 2.4/3.2/4.2.
Abstract methodology severity (BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR) lives here; the finding_add critical/high/medium/low mapping is S2 (do not leak it into S0).
drivers: no downstream story may need a schema change
S1/S2/S3 must build in parallel off a frozen surface
the canonical order must be one declared source of truth

options.name: types-and-mode-interface-module
pros: single source of truth every story imports
drift-proof canonical order via a declared constant
cons: an extra module with no behavior yet

options.name: inline-types-per-story
cons: each impl story re-declares schemas -> drift; no frozen surface -> the program is not contract-first; exactly what the spec section 5 forbids

rationale: A single types-only core/adversarial-review.ts encoding the frozen Finding/Verdict/lens-set/critic-IO schemas + the canonical round order as a declared constant gives S1-S4 one stable import surface and makes drift mechanically detectable, which is the entire point of the spec section 5 contract-first shape (proven by the parallel-decomposition Story 0). Inline per-story types would re-introduce the drift the program exists to prevent.

preMortem.scenario: A schema field diverges from the spec (wrong severity union, missing Finding field), so S1/S2 build against a wrong contract and need a schema change later
preMortem.trigger: transcribing sections 2.2/2.3 loosely instead of verbatim
preMortem.consequence: the acceptance (no downstream schema change) fails; S1-S4 churn
preMortem.mitigation: the smoke asserts the exact field set + the exact severity unions ({BLOCKER,MAJOR,MINOR} / {...,NOT_A_DEFECT}) against the spec; a reviewer diffs the module vs section 2 verbatim

preMortem.scenario: S0 accidentally includes behavior (e.g. a finding_add mapping or a real verifier), violating types-only and pre-empting S2
preMortem.trigger: adding a convenience function to the contract module
preMortem.consequence: scope creep into S2/S4; the parallel build is no longer clean
preMortem.mitigation: scope contract allows only the types module + smoke + config; the module exports types/interfaces/const data only; reviewer confirms zero behavior (no imports of finding_add / no logic)

preMortem.scenario: The canonical order is encoded ambiguously (as prose, or duplicated), so S1-S4 drift from sections 2.4/3.2/4.2
preMortem.trigger: not declaring REVIEW_MODE_PHASES as one constant
preMortem.consequence: the integration order diverges from the spec the way the spec review itself caught (the round-1 critic-loop contradiction)
preMortem.mitigation: declare REVIEW_MODE_PHASES as a single ordered const tuple; the smoke asserts it equals the canonical 5-step order; S4 will import it
